provenance.note: createAgentMessageChunk omits the messageId key entirely when the argument is falsy, which is why both warning families arrive without one while ordinary answers carry event.itemId. The legacy branches are reached whenever the client has not negotiated the JetBrains-private typed-failure capability, which Open Knowledge never advertises. Only candidates[0] is recorded traffic, from a thread whose meta names the wire-observed version; every Config warning entry is reconstructed from the emission templates above, which were read out of the source-read version. The two agree byte for byte on all three literals.

candidates.name: warning-whose-message-opens-with-a-space
candidates.why: The adapter interpolates the message straight after the literal, so a message with its own leading space yields two spaces after the colon. The literal is still intact and this is still a warning; only the prefix itself is fixed, never what follows it.

multiParagraphWarning.why: A single event whose body reads as chrome followed by prose. The adapter cannot produce this — warnings interpolate only the warning message, and answers are separate events carrying an item id — but if one ever arrived it is classified whole, as one notice, and is NEVER split at the blank line. Carving a leading paragraph out of a larger body would mean reinterpreting arbitrary agent prose, which is the failure mode the complete-envelope rule exists to prevent. The residual is a documented, accepted risk.
